subject.title: test(browser): replace broad win32 skip with dynamic directory symlink check

question: Should maintainers accept this low automation-risk test-gating change after exact-head checks are green, or require native Windows browser-test proof first?
rationale: The code path is narrow and matches a merged sibling pattern, but the PR changes whether a Windows junction-backed test runs and the current proof does not directly show this browser test executing on native Windows.

options.title: Merge after green checks
options.body: Accept the low test-harness risk once exact-head required checks are green because the patch is test-only and follows the merged install-safe-path pattern.

options.title: Request native Windows proof
options.body: Ask for a native Windows focused run of `extensions/browser/src/browser/output-directories.test.ts` if maintainers want direct proof that the junction case runs instead of skipping.

options.title: Hold until checks are refreshed
options.body: Leave the PR open if the failing exact-head checks cannot be rerun, cleared, or confirmed as unrelated main-side noise.

recommendation.title: Merge after green checks
recommendation.body: Accept the low test-harness risk once exact-head required checks are green because the patch is test-only and follows the merged install-safe-path pattern.

likelyOwner.reason: `steipete` is the current assigned reviewer and has adjacent browser output-directory history, making him the best available owner for the merge-risk choice.
